prose.text: IPS Control is the signature half of Firewall Control. {{signature-detection}} {{protocol-coverage}} IPS Control requires Advanced Firewall ([[zia.firewall.licensing:ips-needs-advanced]]). {{per-location}} Forwarding through Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC needs the firewall option enabled first: see [[zia.firewall.traffic-path]].

prose.label: ATP and IPS.
prose.text: {{atp-first}} Whether an ATP block appears in the IPS logs is open {{gap:atp-preempt-in-ips-logs}}.

prose.label: Custom signatures.
prose.text: {{custom-signatures}} {{signature-needs-sid}} {{mcp-signature-tools}} {{create-validates-update-does-not}} The relevant caps are in [[zia.firewall.limits]]. {{two-resources}} The actions an IPS rule can take are in [[zia.firewall.actions]].

checks.do: Whether rules that allow ordinary business traffic sit above the default block, and the rank of each.
Whether the recommended IPS Control policy has been compared with the tenant's policy before enabling.
Whether the tenant also has ATP, since its rules are evaluated first.
Whether a custom signature is accepted by the parser, since its Snort compatibility is open.
Whether the firewall log shows the IPS rule name for a blocked flow.

signature-detection.statement: IPS Control uses signature-based detection over all ports and protocols, with signatures built and updated by Zscaler's security research team plus signatures from industry-leading vendors.

quotes: uses signature-based detection to monitor and protect your network traffic from intrusion over all ports and protocols
Zscaler's IPS Control uses IPS signature rules built and updated by Zscaler's security research team, as well as signatures from industry-leading vendors.

protocol-coverage.statement: IPS Control covers web and non-web traffic: HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, DNS, TCP, UDP and IP-based ports and protocols.

quotes: IPS Control enables you to defend your organization against threats from both web and non-web traffic. This includes protection for HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, DNS, TCP, UDP, and IP-based ports and protocols.

default-blocks-all.statement: Zscaler provides a default IPS rule that blocks all traffic. Rules of higher precedence allow specific traffic past it, for example the IT Security group's traffic matching threats.

quotes: default IPS rule that blocks all traffic
(e.g., IT Security group traffic matching threats)
You can create granular policies of higher precedence (i.e., higher admin rank) than the default rule to explicitly allow specific traffic

atp-first.statement: If a tenant has both IPS Control and Advanced Threat Protection, the rules created for ATP are evaluated first.

quotes: rules created for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first

per-location.statement: IPS Control policies are enabled per location.

quotes: You can enable IPS Control policies for specific locations by configuring the appropriate option for the location.

custom-signatures.statement: Customers can create custom IPS signatures in Snort-like syntax, and the signatures take effect through threat categories referenced by the IPS Control policy.

quotes: industry-standard Snort-like syntax
These signatures should be part of the IPS Control policy using threat categories to be enforced on traffic.
picked up by IPS Control rules that reference the same category.

two-resources.statement: Custom signature definitions and IPS policy rules are separate API resources: definitions at `/ipsSignatureRules` and rules at `/firewallIpsRules`. A rule carries the action and criteria; a definition carries its text, category and enabled state.

quotes: ipsSignaturesEndpoint         = "/zia/api/v1/ipsSignatureRules"
RuleText string `json:"ruleText,omitempty"`
Category *IPSSignatureCategory `json:"category,omitempty"`
Enabled bool `json:"enabled"`
firewallIpsRulesEndpoint = "/zia/api/v1/firewallIpsRules"
Action string `json:"action,omitempty"`
NwServices []common.IDNameExtensions `json:"nwServices,omitempty"`
ThreatCategories []common.IDNameExtensions `json:"threatCategories,omitempty"`

signature-needs-sid.statement: The MCP tool describes a custom signature body as Snort/Suricata syntax that must include a unique `sid:` and `rev:`.

quotes: Snort/Suricata signature body; must include a unique sid: and rev:.

create-validates-update-does-not.statement: The Python SDK validates `rule_text` against the dynamic-validation endpoint before creating a signature, but does not do so on update, because the check would flag the rule's own `sid` as a duplicate. The Terraform provider validates on every create and update.

quotes: is validated against the ZIA dynamic-validation

a duplicate — which on an update is the rule being modified
itself, so a pre-flight check would reject every legitimate update.
The provider validates `rule_text` against the Zscaler validation endpoint on every create and update.

mcp-signature-tools.statement: The MCP tools create a custom IPS signature from `name`, `rule_text` and an optional `description`. Update is a PUT-replace: when the caller omits `name` or `rule_text`, the tool fetches the existing signature and backfills both before sending.

quotes: PUT-replace; backfills name/rule_text
payload.setdefault("name", ed.get("name"))
payload.setdefault("rule_text", ed.get("rule_text") or ed.get("ruleText"))
payload: dict[str, Any] = {"name": args.name, "rule_text": args.rule_text}
description: Annotated[Optional[str], Field(default=None, description="Admin note.")] = None
if "name" not in payload or "rule_text" not in payload:
existing, _, ferr = client.zia.ips_signature_rules.get_ips_signature_rule(args.rule_id)

recommended-policy-view.statement: The IPS Control page lets an admin view the recommended IPS Control policy.

quotes: Click Recommended Policy to view the policy Zscaler recommends.

logging.statement: Threats detected in network traffic are shown under Firewall Insights > Logs, and threats detected in web-only traffic also appear on the Security dashboard. The firewall log records the IPS rule name and whether a custom signature applied.

quotes: Threats detected in your network traffic are displayed under Firewall Insights > Logs.
Threats detected in web-only traffic also appear on the Security dashboard.
| The name of the IPS policy that was applied to the Firewall session
| Indicates if a custom IPS signature rule was applied.

atp-preempt-in-ips-logs.title: Whether an ATP block pre-empting IPS appears in the IPS logs
atp-preempt-in-ips-logs.detail: The old reference said an ATP block that pre-empts an IPS rule never shows in IPS logs and named a log field as the discriminator. No captured source states either. Only the evaluation order is documented.
atp-preempt-in-ips-logs.blocks: debugging a block that matches no IPS rule

continuous-signature-updates.title: How often Zscaler updates IPS signatures and whether operators must act
continuous-signature-updates.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Updated continuously by Zscaler; no operator action needed.' The help capture says Zscaler builds and updates the signatures but gives no cadence or statement about operator action. Resolves with a vendor answer.

snort-subset.title: How much of Snort and Suricata syntax the custom signature parser accepts
snort-subset.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Zscaler's parser is a Snort-subset' and arbitrary public Snort rules should be tested first. The help capture says 'Snort-like' and Terraform says Suricata/Snort. Nothing states whether arbitrary public rules are accepted; the SDK validation endpoint is the only arbiter.
snort-subset.blocks: advising on importing public rule sets
